entries.title: Man charged in Lower West Side fatal stabbing of 86-year-old
entries.summary: <p>A man is facing murder charges in the fatal stabbing of an elderly man in Lower West Side Monday evening, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Alejandro Lozano, 44, is charged with first-degree murder, first-degree attempted murder and an additional murder count with probability of death or great bodily harm, police said.</p><p>Lozano is accused of stabbing an 86-year-old man and a 78-year-old woman, both his upstairs neighbors, during an argument at a residence in the 2100 block of West 19th Street about 8:58 p.m. Monday, according to police.</p><p>The injured woman was taken to Stroger Hospital in fair condition. The wounded 86-year-old died after being taken to Mt. Sinai Hospital.</p><p>Officials said the stabbing was “domestic related.”</p><p>Lozano is scheduled to appear in court Thursday.</p>

entries.title: Luke Glendening follows 'crazy ride' to Blackhawks, who need his faceoff skills
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a> are the latest stop on veteran NHL center Luke Glendening's meandering late-career road.</p><p>"I was talking to my wife [about how] in the last 12 months — well, a little bit more — I've been on three PTOs and waivers twice," Glendening said Wednesday. "It's been a crazy ride. Five different cities. But every day in this league is a blessing."</p><p>He played for the Lightning in 2024-25 and for the Devils and Flyers in 2025-26. Then he rejoined the Lightning for training camp in September on a tryout deal but didn't get signed.</p><p>He inked a new PTO with the Rangers on Oct. 19 and parlayed that into a one-year contract, making four appearances for them. Then he wound up on waivers and was <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/22/blackhawks-claim-luke-glendening-waivers-rangers-faceoffs" >claimed</a> Sunday by the Hawks, with whom he will debut Wednesday against the Kraken.</p><p>It should help Glendening that Hawks coach Jeff Blashill knows him well, having previously coached him with AHL Grand Rapids, with the Red Wings and with the Lightning. It already helped him get this Hawks gig, for one thing.</p><p>Blashill said Glendening is "good at what he's good at," namely three things: winning faceoffs, killing penalties and eating minutes against tough competition. Blashill noted Flyers coach Rick Tocchet deployed Glendening against the Penguins' top forwards in the playoffs last season.</p><p>"Doesn't mean he's going to check the other team's best every night here," Blashill added, "but certainly [he's] somebody I believe can go out and give us real trustworthy minutes."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe height="578" width="325" src="https://www.tiktok.com/player/v1/7712278236528479501?embed_from=oembed&music_info=1&description=1&autoplay=1&muted=1" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; fullscreen; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen loading="lazy"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>Even at age 37, Glendening is still a fast skater. Combined with his physicality, that makes him effective on the forecheck, which is a point of emphasis for the Hawks.</p><p>Veteran winger Jordan Greenway will make his second consecutive appearance Wednesday after three consecutive healthy scratches, but it'll be interesting to see if Glendening's presence displaces Greenway moving forward. Greenway's lack of speed has made his forechecking inconsistent, and he hasn't been as physical as hoped, either.</p><p>It's worth noting Glendening contributes nothing offensively. He entered Wednesday with 16 points in 151 games since the start of 2024-25. But the Hawks aren't expecting that from him anyway.</p><p>The faceoff dot is the most important area where he can help. The Hawks rank last in the league in faceoff percentage, which isn't too surprising considering how young their centers are. They've direly lacked a reliable guy to send out for high-leverage draws on penalty kills or when protecting late leads.</p><p>Glendening, on the other hand, is one of the best active draw-takers in the league, sporting a 55.7% career faceoff percentage. He has been above 52% for 12 consecutive seasons. </p><p>He explained it was a late-blooming skill, considering he was a winger at the University of Michigan. He didn't get moved to center until an ECHL stint with Toledo in 2012.</p><p>"As I moved up, they were like, 'If you can't start figuring out how to win faceoffs, you're not going to be in this league,'" he said. "I didn't have a lot of other desirable attributes, so they were like, 'If you can figure this out, you can find a niche role.' </p><p>"That's why I tried to do. I studied. I'd take them as often as I can in practice. Some nights, it doesn't go your way, so you've got to keep building. There's been nights I've been terrible, and there's been nights I've been good."</p><p>Perhaps the best possible thing Glendening could do is pass along knowledge about some tricks of the faceoff trade to young cornerstone Hawks like Frank Nazar, Anton Frondell and (eventually) Connor Bedard.</p><p>"I can name someone at every stop...whether that be a coach, another player, a GM [or] a skills coach who have poured into me and helped me a little bit," he said. "If I can pass that along, I would love to."</p>

entries.title: DK Heard's clutch free throws seal King's comeback win against De La Salle
entries.summary: <p>It’s been a tumultuous few months for DK Heard. He was a star freshman at Mount Carmel last season, but had to leave at the start of this school year and transferred to King, which is extremely close to his home.</p><p>There is always drama around a transfer that takes place shortly before the season begins, and perhaps weathering all that helped Heard focus with the game on the line, the crowd roaring, and De La Salle calling multiple timeouts to ice him at the free-throw line on <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/high-school-basketball/scores/2026/11/25/illinois-high-school-basketball-scores-chicago" >Wednesday</a>.</p><p>Heard had a rough day at the line overall, but he made two free throws when it counted, sinking both with 0.3 seconds left to give the visiting <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/super-25-basketball-rankings/2026/11/17/michael-obriens-preseason-super-25-illinois-high-school-basketball-rankings" >No. 21 Jaguars</a> a 59-58 win.</p><p>“I had to win the game for my team,” Heard said. “That was it. [The timeouts] didn’t impact me at all. I knew I was going to knock the free throws down.”</p><p>Heard went 3-for-9 from the line before hitting the game-winners.</p><p>“I had no doubt in my mind that DK Heard was going to make those two free throws at the end,” King coach Jerell Parker said. “In fact, he came and told me at the five-minute mark that we were going to win the game, that he was going to come up with something big for me.”</p><p>Heard, a 6-4 guard, finished with 19 points and 10 rebounds. He was pitted against his friend and fellow highly-regarded sophomore, 6-7 Zahari Threatt.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-0f0000" name="image-0f0000"></a> <picture data-crop="medium"> <source type="image/webp" width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/ed05fb9/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4730x2655+0+0/resize/490x275!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb0%2F94%2F1506df8048358709bedbf48b4413%2Fob-cst-112626-004.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/853daba/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4730x2655+0+0/resize/980x550!/format/webp/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb0%2F94%2F1506df8048358709bedbf48b4413%2Fob-cst-112626-004.jpg 2x" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <source width="490" height="275" data-srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/27d49d5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4730x2655+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb0%2F94%2F1506df8048358709bedbf48b4413%2Fob-cst-112626-004.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" srcset="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" /> <img class="Image" alt="King’s DK Heard (5) reacts after winning the game against De La Salle. " srcset="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/27d49d5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4730x2655+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb0%2F94%2F1506df8048358709bedbf48b4413%2Fob-cst-112626-004.jpg 1x,https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/c664d99/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4730x2655+0+0/resize/980x550!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb0%2F94%2F1506df8048358709bedbf48b4413%2Fob-cst-112626-004.jpg 2x" width="490" height="275" data-src="https://cst.brightspotcdn.com/dims4/default/27d49d5/2147483647/strip/true/crop/4730x2655+0+0/resize/490x275!/quality/90/?url=https%3A%2F%2Fchorus-production-cst-web.s3.us-east-1.amazonaws.com%2Fbrightspot%2Fb0%2F94%2F1506df8048358709bedbf48b4413%2Fob-cst-112626-004.jpg" data-lazy-load="true" src="data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIHZlcnNpb249IjEuMSIgaGVpZ2h0PSIyNzVweCIgd2lkdGg9IjQ5MHB4Ij48L3N2Zz4=" > </picture> <div class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>King’s DK Heard (5) reacts after winning the game against De La Salle.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Kirsten Stickney/For the Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>King (2-0) trailed 45-37 after three quarters and didn’t take the lead until Heard’s final free throw.</p><p>“I knew at one point we would get in a rhythm,” Parker said. “There were a lot of nerves, a lot of things going on with this ballgame. That’s a really good team we played against with a lot of talent.”</p><p>Threatt finished with 14 points and 11 rebounds. Senior Chaden Harvey scored 16 for De La Salle (1-1) and senior OJ Cross added nine points and 14 rebounds.</p><p>Freshman Jerell Parker Jr., the coach’s son, gave King a huge spark off the bench with 11 points.</p><p>“I coach him like I coach everyone else,” Parker Sr. said. “I see how hard he works at it. He’s up at 6:30 every morning putting up shots and working on his game.</p><p>“The kid has the ultimate confidence and the team has ultimate confidence in him, and as a freshman that means everything.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">DK Heard makes the second FT and King beats De La Salle 59-58. <a href="https://t.co/BJn8pal1uV">pic.twitter.com/BJn8pal1uV</a></p>— Michael O'Brien (@michaelsobrien) <a href="https://x.com/michaelsobrien/status/2125727394182922648?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 25, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>Jacob Wren had 11 points and five rebounds for King, which is enjoying a moment in the city’s high school basketball spotlight for the first time in a couple of decades.</p><p>“This is what high school basketball should feel like,” Parker Sr. said. “Catholic League vs. Public League. This competitive, this kind of crowd, and this environment. It feels good to have King back in the conversation at a really high level. It makes the entire city better."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="HtmlModule"><a class="AnchorLink" id="html-embed-module-bd0000" name="html-embed-module-bd0000"></a><iframe title="No Shot Clock, Ep. 208: The big storylines to follow this season" allowtransparency="true" height="150" width="100%" style="border: none; min-width: min(100%, 430px);height:150px;" scrolling="no" data-name="pb-iframe-player" src="https://www.podbean.com/player-v2/?i=de5mq-1bbc1f3-pb&from=pb6admin&share=1&download=1&rtl=0&fonts=Arial&skin=1&font-color=auto&logo_link=episode_page&btn-skin=c73a3a" loading="lazy"></iframe> </div> </div><p></p>

entries.title: Blackhawks sweep road trip with gritty win over Kraken
entries.summary: <p>SEATTLE — From the moment the NHL schedule was announced in July, it was clear the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks" target="_blank" >Blackhawks</a>' November included both the hardest possible road trip and the easiest possible road trip.</p><p>The hardest trip — against the Panthers, Lightning and Hurricanes — went so badly that it prompted an internal reckoning and a state-of-the-union address by general manager Kyle Davidson.</p><p>It turns out the Hawks just needed the easiest trip to come around. A gritty 3-1 victory over the Kraken on Wednesday completed a three-game Hawks sweep of the Pacific Northwest, following wins over the equally benign <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/21/blackhawks-flames-sam-rinzel-wyatt-kaiser-martin-pospisil" >Flames</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/blackhawks/2026/11/22/blackhawks-canucks-roman-kantserov-hat-trick" >Canucks</a>.</p><p>In a matter of five days, the Hawks' road record improved from 0-8-1 to 3-8-1.</p><p>"There was a lot of buy-in today," said goalie Spencer Knight, who made 29 saves and barely missed out on his first shutout since January. "A lot of commitment to play a good road game and...sticking with it throughout the game. It was fun for me to see."</p><p>Said forward Anton Frondell: "We always knew that we could be this team that we’ve shown the last three games."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Roman Kantserov with one of the most impressive empty-net goals I’ve seen: <a href="https://t.co/6hc3bAu6F7">pic.twitter.com/6hc3bAu6F7</a></p>— Ben Pope (@BenPopeCST) <a href="https://x.com/BenPopeCST/status/2125822976067240288?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">November 26, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p>The Kraken had the majority of possession and outshot the Hawks 30-19, but the visitors generally kept them to the outside and blocked a number of shots that could've further inflated that margin. They were credited with 19 blocks to the Kraken's seven.</p><p>Even Patrick Kane — an unlikely candidate — made a massive block with his right foot in the final minutes, which forced him to the locker room early. Coach Jeff Blashill wasn't sure of Kane's status afterward.</p><p>"Early in the season, we weren't committed enough [to block shots], and I think we've gotten much better at it," Blashill said. "We're in lanes, and we're way more committed to blocking shots. It's one of those things that's a little bit contagious.</p><p>"It doesn't come without some risk, and I certainly don't want a guy like Patrick to miss time or anything like that. But it is part of the game now, and it's part of the commitment to winning that you have to have."</p><p>The game remained goalless into the third period until Cole Smith tipped in an Ethan Del Mastro shot with 14 minutes left.</p><p>Roman Kantserov then extended his NHL rookie goal-scoring lead with two more goals, including an extremely impressive empty-netter where he stripped Kraken forward Matthew Wood deep inside the Hawks' zone, turned and hit the cage from 154 feet away. He's now on a stunning 47-goal pace this season.</p><p>"Those are paces that are hard to keep up, so we'll see," Blashill said. "But he finds ways to score in different ways. Obviously I trust him enough to have him out there five-on-six, as well. He's a good defensive player."</p>
